messages:
alex: quick follow-up from the runtime probe canary. ran the sm-capability gate across A100 / H100 / L4 and saw unexpected fallbacks on a subset of H100 nodes when sequence length hits certain boundaries.

alex: details: most requests used attention_fused (fast path) but ~8% on H100 fell back to attention_split_kv (slower). not correlated with load, looked like a capability detection quirk.

devon: do you have the probe logs? was it the initial probe or the runtime re-check?

alex: pasted below — it’s from the startup probe and again during runtime re-eval.

alex: ```
[probe] node=h100-03 sm_cap_check: bf16=true, fp8=false, tensorcore_level=SM90
[probe] kernel_select: attention_fused -> enabled
[run] seq_len=65 kernels: attention_fused failed -> reason: launchFailure(code=5)
[run] fallback -> attention_split_kv, latency +18%
[probe] runtime_reprobe: sm_reported=bf16=true, but probe_microbench shows lower throughput than expected
```

maria: hmm. launchFailure(code=5) usually indicates mismatched shared memory usage or a kernel selector assuming a capability that's borderline. could be an H100 driver firmware edge. did you capture driver versions?

alex: yes — all H100s are on nvidia-driver 535.112.03, cuda 12.2. reboots didn't fix it. A100 machines show no failures.

devon: two hypotheses: 1) our SM capability gating is too binary (we treat bf16 true => pick fused kernel) and we should add a microbench check that validates actual kernel launch/throughput, or 2) the fused kernel has a codepath that hits a rare warp-scheduling condition on SM90 when seq_len mod 64 == 1.

jen: conservative ask: we need correctness before perf. if fused kernel can legitimately fail on some H100s, we must ensure automatic fallback always preserves correctness and we add alerting when fallback rate crosses threshold.

maria: agreed. proposal: make gating two-stage — capability flag from driver + a fast microbench probe (single-shot) that runs a tiny fused launch with the typical seq shapes. only enable fused if both pass. also record a per-node probe score.

alex: sounds good. microbench can be super lightweight (1 launch, 1 token). we already have code for `probe_small` in runtime/bench. re-use that and add shape variants [32,64,65,128].

devon: downside: extra probe adds ~30-50ms to node startup. for Dedicated pools that's fine, for hosted cold starts might be annoying. we could cache probe results per-node and only re-probe on kernel updates or driver changes.

maria: yep cache + TTL 24h and invalidate on driver/kernel update events. also emit metrics: probe_ok (bool), fallback_rate (p50 over 5m).

infra-bot: automated check results: probe_small executed on 12 h100 nodes: 10 passed, 2 flaky (failed on seq_len=65). Logged as infra-ticket INF-4821.

alex: action items: 1) devon to implement microbench gating + cache (PR), 2) maria to add metrics and alert (fallback_rate > 2% -> page), 3) jen to add canary policy to block fused reduction until probe coverage > 90% across regions.

devon: I'll own the PR. will add a debug flag so we can force microbench off in stress runs. aiming for a small patch this week.

maria: I'll sketch the alert query: `sum(rate(kernel_fallback_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kernel_launch_total[5m])) > 0.02` then route to oncall.

jen: also add a note in the rollout doc: when we flip fused on, do progressive rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks on fallback_rate and avg latency.

alex: one more thought — for L4 we shouldn't microbench for bf16 since L4 inference path is already quantized fallback-heavy. keep probe only for SM90+ families.

devon: makes sense. implement family filter: if gpu_family in [H100, A100] run microbench, else skip.

alex: thanks all. I'll update the RFC follow-up doc with these decisions and link the INF ticket. :white_check_mark: :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — @devon please ping when you have a draft so we can iterate on the metric labels and alerts.

devon: will do.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary assign: h100-pool-2 -> probe_small enabled (gradual).
